bonsaiEditSession.toolchain: ifcopenshell.api 0.8.5 (the API core Bonsai's Blender tools drive)

evaluationMode: in-sandbox: install-feasibility measurement + API-level equivalence via ifcopenshell.api (the core Bonsai drives) + docs-level desktop workflow analysis; GUI inspection REFUSED (headless sandbox)

forkGateAssessment.blender: NOT justified: every capability this spike needed from the desktop surface (pset editing, moving, adding, saving) is delivered by the existing ifcopenshell.api + Blender's native API; no §6(1) required-capability gap was found
forkGateAssessment.bonsai: NOT justified: Bonsai's value is the Blender-side UX over the same IfcOpenShell core this spike exercises; the adapter boundary stays at the file/API level

installFeasibility.bonsaiAddonInstallable: REFUSED: the Bonsai add-on is not a pip package — it ships through Blender's extension platform or the IfcOpenShell repository, requiring a Blender installation and a display

pipInstallBpy.classification: REFUSED (headless Blender not installable on this interpreter)
pipInstallBpy.outcome: REFUSED: 'No matching distribution found for bpy' — Blender's bpy wheels target the Python version Blender embeds (3.11 line), not 3.12

blender.adapterImplication: running Blender as a SEPARATE PROCESS (the desktop adapter model) keeps GPL obligations inside the Blender process; embedding bpy in-process would import GPL terms into the host
blender.evidence: docs-level citation: https://www.blender.org/about/license/ — verify before adoption

bonsai.evidence: docs-level citation: https://bonsaibim.org/ and the IfcOpenShell repository — verify the add-on's license block before adoption
bonsai.license: distributed within the IfcOpenShell project (LGPL-3.0-or-later per its repository)

projectionArtifacts.reason: opening voiding a mapped host / filled by a mapped element (the fenestration op creates its own void)

verificationThroughNeutralReader.readerGate: the provider-neutral reader flags desktop-authored elements without an AISE mapping as external additions — they never silently merge into the Reality Graph; an explicit AISE-side decision (import review) is required
